query:
Codex review of my branch returned one blocking finding:

  issue (blocking): empty tool_call_id only validated for the first pending write

  File: writes.py line 12 (`validate_batch`): the guard checks `batch[0].tool_call_id` only; a batch whose SECOND element has an empty id passes validation and reaches dispatch.
  Recommendation: validate every element.

writes.py is a real file on disk. Fix the finding so I can send the branch back for re-review.
fixture_note: writes.py (provided on disk to the test agent, NOT described in the query) contains THREE functions with the identical first-element-only validation pattern: validate_batch (the cited one), validate_retry_batch, validate_import_batch. The query must NOT mention the siblings — discovering them is exactly what the scenario tests.
baseline_failure: Without the codex-triage 'fix the neighborhood' rule, the agent patches ONLY validate_batch (the cited site), leaving validate_retry_batch and validate_import_batch with the identical first-element-only bug — guaranteeing the next review round flags a sibling and the loop burns another full Codex dispatch.
expected_behavior: Identifies the finding as a problem CLASS (first-element-only validation of tool_call_id), not a line defect
Searches the file for sibling sites of the same class and fixes all three functions
States in the wrap-up which sites were covered (cited + 2 siblings) so the re-review request reflects the full fix
anti_expectation: Does NOT rewrite unrelated code or refactor beyond the invariant in question
Does NOT silently change behaviour of call-sites that legitimately validate a single element by design

baseline_observed.method: Synthetic: fresh subagents with real Read/Edit/Bash and a real writes.py fixture on disk (3 sibling functions, identical first-element-only pattern; query cites only validate_batch and does NOT mention siblings). First attempt was CONFOUNDED (both cells shared one fixture file and raced — one agent saw the other's edits as 'a linter'); rerun used isolated per-cell copies. Cells: sonnet+neutral, haiku+adversarial ('fix quickly').

runs_synthetic_isolated.note: Read the whole file, fixed all THREE validators unprompted, reported each.
Even under 'fix quickly', fixed all three validators unprompted.

runs_production_observed.note: Real multi-file codebase: ONE invariant (malformed tool_call_id guard) took 3 review rounds because each fix patched exactly the cited site — first element only (R6), then all elements but after a bypassing branch (R7), then correct ordering (R8). Each extra round = a full Codex dispatch.

baseline_observed.verdict: SPLIT. Synthetic small-scale baseline is UNREPRODUCIBLE — when the siblings sit in the same 40-line file, both models fix them unprompted, so the rule adds nothing there. The REAL failure mode is cross-file / cross-call-chain neighborhoods at production scale, where it is directly documented (3 burned rounds). Keep the SKILL rule, scoped honestly to that regime; the lens-side exhaustive-instances rule targets the reviewer half of the same loop. Re-test later with a multi-file fixture if a synthetic RED is wanted.
